<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da93a8b3e0bfa0ac5d4d68059b419435eb7c8371` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `de1923a0ca5a31e8c0c525ba937d9ab6f46b8205` — the merge of head `43cf17d79b21cbef2ff9d3631d8569013ba89039` into base `da93a8b3e0bfa0ac5d4d68059b419435eb7c8371`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin de1923a0ca5a31e8c0c525ba937d9ab6f46b8205 && git checkout de1923a0ca5a31e8c0c525ba937d9ab6f46b8205
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin da93a8b3e0bfa0ac5d4d68059b419435eb7c8371 43cf17d79b21cbef2ff9d3631d8569013ba89039 && git checkout -B drift-repro da93a8b3e0bfa0ac5d4d68059b419435eb7c8371 && git merge --no-ff 43cf17d79b21cbef2ff9d3631d8569013ba89039

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da93a8b3e0bfa0ac5d4d68059b419435eb7c8371
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs da93a8b3e0bfa0ac5d4d68059b419435eb7c8371` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `43cf17d79b21cbef2ff9d3631d8569013ba89039`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20862 (body; triage grade `5912757695`; the seat's claim `5913606714`; the dev's `os-dev-report` `5916095165`), the prior landings PR #20817 (#20679) and PR #20853 (#20761, the maintainer's ruling `5904938166` rule 2 and rule 3), PR #20907's body and file list (5 files, +674/-59, head repo = base repo, draft), the net diff against the merge-base `ca5408c62` (the merge `a783880517`'s second parent, so the diff is exactly the five files), and the head's check-runs. Source read at the head by sha: the automation domain, the metadata protocol's save and delete, the sys_metadata repository, the objectql registry, the automation engine and plugin, and the flow precedence resolver. Nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated here.

Check-runs on the head, collapsed to latest per name, all converged: 35 runs, 32 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, none of them required). The seven required contexts are all `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. `Check Changeset` is `success`. The file list touches no governed surface.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) One save path, same scope, same publish mode — right.** At the head the domain holds exactly one `saveMetaItem` call site and exactly one `deleteMetaItem` call site (base: one save site, in the clone arm; no delete site). `registerAndSaveFlow` is module-private (no export), as are `unregisterAndDeleteFlow`, `restoreFlowRegistration` and the two helper types, so nothing widens the package surface. The save is `saveMetaItem({ type: 'flow', name, item })` — no organization, no package, no mode — which is byte-for-byte the clone arm's call at the base: env-wide (the repository targets the `package_id IS NULL` row), the protocol's default mode is `publish` (protocol line 16605), so the row lands `active`, and the registry write-through registers it as a runtime row. `saveMetaItem` is consulted, not edited (no metadata-protocol file in the diff). The three doors (create, update, clone) all go through the helper, so they cannot drift.

Clone door behaviour: unchanged on every single-request path. At the base the clone arm resolved the protocol, registered, saved, and on a failed save unregistered the target; at the head the helper resolves the protocol first (same position), adds one read probe (`getFlow` on the target name, which the collision probe just proved absent, so `held` is null), registers, saves, and on a failed save takes the `held`-is-null branch of `restoreFlowRegistration`, which is `unregisterFlow` — the base's undo. The response is still the served clone plus the notice. The only measurable difference is one extra engine read on the target name.

**(b) Order and rollback — consistent; the "held definition back" reading is right.** Engine first: `registerFlow` runs inside the helper's `try`, a throw is answered through `flowDefinitionRefusal` as `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, and the store is never reached (runtime pin: `saveMetaItem` not called). Store second: a throw from `saveMetaItem` is relayed through `errorFromThrown` with the store's own code and status (measured on the showcase: `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, `422 INVALID_METADATA`), and the engine is restored: a name the engine did not hold is unregistered; a name it held gets `held` re-registered, where `held` is the engine's own in-process parsed copy (`getFlow` returns the raw `FlowParsed`, credentials intact — not the served projection), re-run through `registerFlow`'s validators and trigger re-arm, the same idempotent path the boot pull and the reload re-sync take. Reading the claim's "a failed save withdraws the engine registration" as "withdraws THIS request's registration" is the only reading consistent with the card's own defect statement: unregistering an already-held name on a refused update would take a live, stored flow out of the engine until the next boot, i.e. a refusal that also loses a flow the store still holds. After a refused update the engine and the store both hold the previous definition. Pinned in both files (identity `toBe(before)` in the runtime pin; the previous label on `/automation` and on `/meta` after a gate-refused update in the booted pin) and by the dev's third ablation (restore disabled: 1 of 11 red).

Where engine and store can still disagree: (i) a `saveMetaItem` that throws after `repo.put` landed (audit, projector or event tail) leaves the row while the engine is put back, and (ii) the DELETE mirror, a `deleteMetaItem` that throws after the row was removed while the engine re-registers the flow — in both the caller gets an error, and the next boot binds the store. Both are the protocol's own post-persist tail and have the same shape the clone arm already carried at the base; the door does not open a new one. (iii) `restoreFlowRegistration` is not inside a try: a throw from re-registering `held` would leave this request's definition registered — unreachable in practice, since `held` passed these same validators in this process. On the DELETE undo the engine re-derives its state through `registerFlow` (status-disabled from the definition, trigger re-armed, the scheduled-work policy re-judged at arming), and the durable enable state lives in the ledger map that `withdrawFlow` does not clear, so a flow put back keeps its enable state. None of this is a defect of the order chosen; all of it is observation, not filed (no measured reach).

**(c) The refusals in front stay in front — right, on all three doors plus DELETE.** Create: `refuseUnauthoredFlowWrite` (the #20853 rule, which itself reuses #20679's `packagedBaseRefusal`) is asked before `keepStoredFlowCredentials` and before the helper. Update: the same, after the envelope check, as on `/meta`. Clone: the same, after the source and collision probes. DELETE: `refusePackagedFlowBaseChange(…, 'delete')` before `unregisterAndDeleteFlow`, so a locked base (`403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`) is refused before the engine's own `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` and before any store call. Neither the engine nor the store is reached on a refusal — pinned (runtime: `registerFlow` and `saveMetaItem` never called for a packaged name and for a claimed package; dogfood control: `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` on the update door and on a create onto the packaged name, definition byte-identical after). The store asks the same one rule again inside `saveMetaItem` — a second ask of one function, no second implementation. The no-protocol fallback (engine-only registration and removal) is right and matches the posture the two front refusals and the base clone arm documented: a composition with no metadata store has nothing to persist into and no `/meta` door to be at parity with; a slot that is wired and fails to resolve still fails loud through `resolveServiceOrLoud` (the lock pin's composition-edge case, unchanged). Pinned in both directions (create and delete).

**(d) The DELETE arm — required, the protocol's own path, no reach beyond `/meta`'s.** Required: the dev measured on `1921e7e3e2` (create and update durable, DELETE unchanged) that a flow created then deleted through the door read `200` on `/meta` and `200` on `/automation` after the cold boot — with durable creates, an engine-only DELETE is the card's defect in the other direction (a `200` for a removal the platform does not keep), so the change makes it necessary; it stays inside the claim's file surface. Protocol's own path: `deleteMetaItem({ type: 'flow', name })` — no organization, no state, no package — is the same call the REST `/meta` DELETE route sends without a state (that route adds only the org scope its helper derives, which for a type with no per-org channel is env-wide, plus optional parent-version, actor and storage-drop extras). Reach: it removes the ACTIVE overlay row of that name; a pending draft survives, exactly as `/meta`'s delete without a state. A packaged flow's artifact definition is never a row `deleteMetaItem` can remove: for a packaged name the lock answers first; under the operator hatch the protocol's removal helper admits it, finds no overlay row, answers "already at artifact default" success and restores the artifact's registry view — so the door still unregisters the engine copy as it did before and touches no artifact, and the next boot binds the artifact again as before. A tenant row bound to a package is reachable — `deleteMetaItem` without a package resolves "any package" (the repository's documented fallback) — exactly as `/meta` DELETE without a state does today; nothing beyond it. Order and undo mirror the write path; pinned in both files and by ablation (delete call removed: 2 of 11 red).

**(e) The changeset — accurate, matches the diff, claims nothing undelivered, carries the fix.** `'@objectstack/runtime': minor`, a `fix(runtime)!:` title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, a `**BREAKING**` banner, and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — a category in the gate's closed vocabulary, and the right one: no stored row changes shape and nothing an author wrote is renamed or removed. Every prose bullet corresponds to a code path read above: env-wide live save through `saveMetaItem`; engine first with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`; a store refusal relayed with its own code and status, a create withdrawn, an update put back; DELETE through `deleteMetaItem` with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` still first, a name with no row removed as before, a refused delete put back and relayed; the two front refusals unchanged; no protocol, engine-only. The stated narrowing (two bodies `200` → `400 INVALID_REQUEST` / `422 INVALID_METADATA`) is the measured pair, labelled as measured, under a generic sentence that declares the whole class ("refuse a definition the metadata store refuses"). The migration line gives the one-line fix per case: rename to a name starting with a letter; fix the definition as the gate's finding says.

### ② Semver level

The narrowing is real: both measured bodies were engine-accepted and store-refused before, so the doors answered `200` for them; now the door answers the store's refusal. Complete list: the measured pair is not the exhaustive set of store refusals the doors can now relay — by source reading, on an environment kernel the protocol's per-item lock (`403 ITEM_LOCKED`) and the protocol's layered-envelope-body refusal (`422 INVALID_METADATA`) are also newly reachable through these doors, `403 NOT_CREATABLE` is not (the `flow` type allows runtime creation), and `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` was already in front. The changeset declares the class in its generic sentence and enumerates the measured members as measured, which is the right shape; the class is what the accept set moved by.

`no (narrowing)` + `minor` + BREAKING is right under the changeset rule: the value answers whether the accept set widens — nothing widens here (no new route, body, export or code) — and `(narrowing)` is the one arm the closed pair allows beside it; a narrowing is BREAKING and so owes the banner, the bang, at least `minor` under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major`), the migration line and one ADR-0087 disposition — all present, and both gates are green on the head. The claim's `Clause-②: no` was a pre-diff reading with the dev instructed to re-read against the measured diff; the re-declaration is the measured one.

### ③ Boundary flags

Deviations:

- **DELETE arm (beyond the claim's enumerated arms).** Answered in ①(d): required by the change, the protocol's own path, same reach as `/meta` DELETE without a state, inside the claim's file surface, pinned in both new files and by ablation. Accepted.
- **Edit to `automation-packaged-base-lock.test.ts` outside the named pin files.** Measured necessity (four success-path cases now reach the real `saveMetaItem` over a store-less harness and answered `500`); +16/-0, harness `standInStore()` plus four call sites, no assertion changed; the file's own clone case already stood the store in identically at the base; the composition-edge controls (no protocol; a wired slot that fails to resolve does not fail open) are untouched. Accepted. Coverage note, not a defect: the hatch case now stands the store in, so an operator-hatch overlay write through `/automation` has no real-store pin at door level (the booted pin does not exercise the hatch).
- **Clause-② re-declaration.** Right — ②.
- **Failed-update reading.** Right — ①(b).
- **One merge of main (`a783880517`).** Its second parent is the merge-base, the net diff is the five files, CI measured the merge ref on this head; `origin/main` moving 11 commits since (one gate-input baseline this diff does not touch) changes no judgment here. Accepted.

Out-of-scope findings (all `carrier: none`, noted, not filed):

1. **Update through the automation door beside a `/meta` row bound to a package.** Source reading at the head confirms the first half: the repository keys rows by (org, type, name, package), a package-less save targets the `package_id IS NULL` row, so the update lands as a second row beside the bound one. The second half is not resolvable by source reading either: at boot both rows hydrate into the registry under the bare name (the hydration registers without a package id), so the later-hydrated row overwrites the earlier one in store-read order and the precedence resolver receives only one contender — the winner is order-dependent, not the resolver's rank. Pre-existing on a bare `/meta` PUT (same put, same hydration); this PR gives the door parity with it, and an update that used to be lost outright after a boot is now at worst an order-dependent tie. Not filed is right under the filing gate: no measured reach. It is a source-read metadata-authoring trap on the `/meta` door first, and belongs with the flow-precedence work this seat holds; a card once measured, on that door.
2. **`FlowSchema.name` admits a leading underscore the item-name grammar refuses.** This one has a measured reach: the booted pin measured the door refusing a name the spec admits (`400 INVALID_REQUEST`), so a flow shipped in code under such a name loads and registers while no runtime door can ever persist it — declared but not enforced, on `packages/spec`. The refusal is loud and prescriptive, so it is not a silent trap and the dev was right not to touch spec inside this file surface; but it is a spec-lane card (narrow the flow name grammar to the item-name grammar, the ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove route), not a PR note. Escalated to the seat to file.
3. **DELETE removes the active row only; a pending draft survives.** Same contract as `/meta` DELETE without a state; the automation door has no draft concept (its save is live). Not filed is right: no measured reach beyond the `/meta` contract it mirrors.
4. **Putting back a held definition adds one in-memory version-history entry.** No door serves it; `withdrawFlow` resets it. Not filed is right.

Reviewer's own observations, not filed: the post-persist throw windows in ①(b), the protocol's tail and not the door's; the hatch coverage note above.
